name: Roasted Broccoli with Lemon and Garlic
pitch: This simple side comes together with what you've got, and if you have a lemon or even a splash of vinegar hiding in the fridge, it really ties the whole thing together.
steps: Toss your broccoli florets in a large bowl with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper, and a clove or two of garlic if you have it — or just skip it, it'll still be tasty.
Spread the broccoli in a single layer on a baking sheet — don't crowd it or it'll steam instead of roast.
Roast for 15–20 minutes until the edges are a little crispy and you can poke the stems with a fork.
Squeeze a bit of lemon juice over the top if you have one — or a small splash of white vinegar works in a pinch. Serve alongside your tofu.

name: Crispy Tofu and Roasted Broccoli Bowl
pitch: You've got both main players right here — tofu and broccoli roast up beautifully together and make a genuinely satisfying weeknight bowl.
steps: Preheat your oven to 400°F. Press your tofu if you have a minute — wrap it in a clean dish towel and set something heavy on it for 5–10 minutes to get some moisture out.
Cut the tofu into cubes and your broccoli into bite-sized pieces. Spread them out on a sheet pan — keep them in a single layer so they roast, not steam.
Drizzle everything lightly with oil and season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of red pepper flakes if you have them. A little soy sauce over the tofu adds great flavor.
Roast for about 20–25 minutes, giving the pan a shake halfway through, until the broccoli edges are a little crispy and the tofu is golden.
Serve over rice or noodles if you have them, or just as-is — simple but satisfying.

name: Garlic Soy Tofu & Broccoli Stir-Fry
pitch: This is a simple, satisfying weeknight staple — crispy tofu and tender broccoli tossed in a savory garlic-soy sauce that comes together in no time.
steps: Press the tofu for 10 minutes by wrapping it in a clean towel and setting something heavy on top, then cut it into bite-sized cubes.
Heat a generous splash of oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and let it cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crispy, then set aside.
In the same pan, add a little more oil and toss in the broccoli florets. Stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Add 2–3 minced garlic cloves and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the tofu to the pan and pour over a sauce made from 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon vinegar, and a pinch of pepper. Toss everything together and cook for 1–2 more minutes.
Serve as-is or over rice or noodles if you have them — it's honestly great either way.
toolSuggestion: A large non-stick skillet or wok
